newsitem.title: UK: Pearson up after reorganisation report.
newsitem.headline: Pearson up after reorganisation report.

text.p: Shares in Pearson Plc rose in early trading on Tuesday after a UK newspaper report said the company could launch a major overhaul as early as next month.
The stock was up 6-1/2p at 713 by 0738 GMT.
A report in the Independent newspaper said Pearson would begin a round of strategy meetings on January 8, the day on which Marjorie Scardino takes over as chief executive.
The newspaper said the meetings would consider the future of Pearson's television interests and that the company was also considering the sale of its 50 percent stake in investment bank Lazard.

Media analysts said the move had been expected. "A strategic review at Pearson has been mooted for some time," said one market watcher who added that the issue had dampened the company's share performance, beause it was seen as overdue.

Scardino met with analysts in the autumn just after her appointment was announced and made a "favourable impression" said one attendee of the meeting. She will replace the outgoing Frank Barlow. On Monday, Pearson announced it would be buying a stake in two South African business publications as part of its strategy to gain a foothold in key financial markets.
The deal, woth 11.5 million pounds, was for a 50 percent stake in the Business Day and Financial Mail newspapers.
